text: A digital repeater regenerates a signal; an analog amplifier boosts it. What is the consequence?
choices: The repeater discards accumulated noise by re-deciding each symbol, while the amplifier amplifies signal and noise together
There is no practical difference over short distances
explanation: Regeneration re-decides which discrete value was sent and emits a clean signal; noise does not accumulate across hops. Amplification scales everything present, so noise compounds — which is why a transcontinental analog call sounded the way it did and a digital one does not.
